issue:
I'm noticing that you all have many default versions of roles. (e.g. front end developer for react, angular, vue.js, etc.) What do you consider best practice 
for when to create a new test versus create a variant of the test? What are the advantages and disadvantages of using variants?
subject:
When should I create a variant versus
 have a different test?
response: According to our release notes, you can create a variant of an existing test when you want to offer different versions of a test with varying levels of difficulty or content. This is useful when you have multiple roles with similar requirements but different technologies. Creating a variant is more efficient than creating a new test from scratch. For more information, see [Creating test variants](https://support.hackerrank.com/articles/7530103378).
justification: The article provides guidance on when to create a variant versus a new test, including the advantages and disadvantages of using variants. [cite:verified]

issue:

We have sent a candidate a Hackerrank assessment already, but we have been informed that they require extra time. As the assessment is 105 minutes, they need an extra 50% extra time added (so around 53 minutes) in addition.

Please can you provide step-by-step instruction on how we are to reinvite them.

Do we find their profile in 'Candidates' , put in Add time 53 minutes and then click 'reinvite' and send the email? The email to the candidate says 105 minutes as the duration though still so not sure how we can check?

Thanks
subject:
How to reinvite candidate to Hackerrank 
assessment and add extra time
response: To add extra time for a candidate, you need to reinvite them to the assessment. To do this, go to the 'Candidates' tab, select the candidate, click 'More' and then 'Add Time'. Enter the additional time required and click 'Confirm'. The candidate will receive an email with the updated duration.
justification: According to the article 'Adding extra time for candidates', you can add extra time by reinviting the candidate to the assessment. The article provides step-by-step instructions on how to do this. [cite:verified]
